items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-bone script; the source record identifies specimen 前2.32.4 / 合37459
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 八 in Shang oracle script, linked to Academia Sinica specimen 前2.32.4 / 合37459. Oracle-bone examples are cataloged in the period as numerals; the graph's proposed separation origin remains debated.
items.alt: Two diverging strokes redrawn as an oracle-script glyph for 八.
items.selection_reason: A usable early-form candidate with unusually specific specimen provenance and stated CC0 reuse. It illustrates the early graph without claiming that the strokes depict a confirmed object.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated for the redraw and source picture on the Commons file page.

items.period: Warring States period bronze-script style; source cited as 丙辰方壺 西清19·3
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 八 in Warring States bronze-script style, sourced by Commons to 丙辰方壺 西清19·3. It offers a later comparison with the Shang oracle-script redraw; it is not an artifact photograph.
items.alt: A two-stroke 八 glyph in Warring States bronze-script style, represented as a vector redraw.
items.selection_reason: A second sourced period example shows a later script tradition and has an explicit source-object citation and public-domain release.
items.rights: Public domain; the Commons page states that the modern vector representation is released for unrestricted reuse.

limitations.text: Both candidates are modern vector redrawings, not photographs. This researcher did not inspect their pixels; visual selection and any shape-specific caption claims require the separate visual review.

The oracle file is directly tied to an Academia Sinica glyph record; the Warring States file cites a vessel source and paleographic databases. These descriptions establish candidates and provenance, not independent confirmation of every historical interpretation attached to 八.
